solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pit to accommodate fantastic bowler in major group

indicators.note: to accommodate means to take something in, so the pit holds the other piece

parts.note: a pock is a small pit or hollow, as in a pockmark

indicators.note: fantastic suggests something wildly fanciful, so the letters of bowler are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mine pit making room for a remarkable bowler who is part of a major sporting group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowler' tempts as cricket or a hat; it is just six letters for 'fantastic' to scramble before 'to accommodate' lodges them.
explanation.definitionFit: A power bloc is an alliance of nations or interests wielding great influence, a major grouping.

clue.text: Music maker and fashion designer wasting day in boat essentially

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
the essence is the core, so the middle letters of the word
wasting means losing, so a letter is lost

parts.note: Pierre Cardin was a French fashion designer

explanation.surface: A musician and a couturier idle away a day aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' keeps the core of the boat, dropping its ends; 'wasting' sheds the day from the designer, Pierre Cardin, before 'in' puts him aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocarina is a small egg-shaped wind instrument, something that makes music.

clue.text: Dash with director to see African animal

parts.note: elan is flair or dash

explanation.surface: Racing off with a film director to spot wildlife in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is a large antelope of the African savanna.

clue.text: Moneybags with no end of dollars represented dreaded character

indicators.note: re-presented, laid out again in another order
with no means without, so a letter is removed
the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A rich man who has lost his last dollar is now portrayed as a villain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' removes S ('end of dollars') from MONEYBAGS; 'represented' rearranges the remaining MONEYBAG.
explanation.definitionFit: The bogeyman is an imaginary monster used to frighten children, a figure of dread.

clue.text: How one might describe Conservative with record likely to succeed?

parts.note: a Conservative politician sits on the right of the political spectrum
a track is one recording on an album

explanation.surface: A Tory with a good track record seems bound to do well.
explanation.walkthrough: The Conservatives are Britain's main right-of-centre party.
explanation.definitionFit: On the right track is an idiom for proceeding correctly and so heading towards success.

clue.text: Youngster carrying odd bits of litter in Highland dress?

indicators.note: carrying means holding within, so the other piece goes inside

parts.note: a kid is a child

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters: first, third, fifth

explanation.surface: A child picking up scraps of rubbish while in Scottish costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd bits of' means the first, third and fifth letters; 'carrying' has the child hold them. The kilt is traditional Scottish Highland dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Kilted means wearing a kilt, the pleated tartan skirt of traditional Scottish costume.

clue.text: Choice film for an audience

indicators.note: an audience hears rather than reads, so the word is what is said aloud

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a film

explanation.surface: Selecting a movie that will suit the viewers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for an audience' signals a homophone: PIC, said aloud, gives PICK.
explanation.definitionFit: Your pick is your preferred selection, the option you have chosen.

clue.text: Gamble on a boxing match and behave irresponsibly

parts.note: to play is to bet, as in playing the tables
a bout is a contest in the ring

explanation.surface: Betting on a prizefight is reckless behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: To play about is to mess around, acting frivolously instead of sensibly.

clue.text: Pass time around hotel making complaint

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Whiling away time near the hotel and grumbling about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts H inside COL. 'Complaint' means an illness here, not a grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Cholera is a serious intestinal disease, and complaint can mean a bodily ailment.

clue.text: Slang, say, on a regular basis in extended story

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals: the first, third, fifth and so on

explanation.surface: Using slang now and then while telling a long tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on a regular basis' takes the odd letters of SLANG SAY: S, A, G, A.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga is a long narrative, originally a Norse heroic tale, now any lengthy account.

clue.text: Pay attention to a floodgate when broken

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the letters are reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: Look at that burst floodgate!
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' is the anagram signal on A FLOODGATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Get a load of is an informal exclamation urging someone to look at or notice something.

clue.text: Benign family in appropriate fashion overlooking first sign of unfriendliness

parts.note: kin means one's relatives

indicators.note: overlooking means leaving out, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: duly means properly, in the fitting way

indicators.note: the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A kind family behaving properly and ignoring any hint of hostility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overlooking' removes U (the first sign of 'unfriendliness') from DULY, leaving DLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindly as an adjective means warm-hearted and gentle, a close synonym of benign.

clue.text: High tax dividing European city endlessly

indicators.note: the tax splits the other letters apart by sitting inside them
without its end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: Leeds is a city in Yorkshire, northern England
VAT is value added tax, a UK sales tax

explanation.surface: A steep levy splitting a European city's finances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the city's last letter and 'dividing' splits what is left with the tax. Leeds is a city in Yorkshire; VAT is Britain's sales tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Elevated means raised up, at a great height, so it matches high.

clue.text: Horse taken by a British writer in Asian city

parts.note: a nag is an old or worn-out horse
Saki was the pen name of H. H. Munro, British short-story writer

explanation.surface: A horse being ridden by a British author somewhere in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: Saki is the pen name of the Edwardian short-story writer H. H. Munro.
explanation.definitionFit: Nagasaki is a port city in southern Japan, on the island of Kyushu.

clue.text: A large French department satisfied about new place for cultivation

parts.note: the Lot is a département in south-west France

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: met as in met a need, fulfilled it

explanation.surface: A big French administrative region pleased with a new site for growing crops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts N inside MET.
explanation.definitionFit: An allotment is a small plot of land rented for growing vegetables, common in Britain.

clue.text: Part of boom anticipated in ME country

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A boom expected in some Middle Eastern economy.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'in', but 'in ME country' cannot stand for the answer; 'in' is a link word. ME is the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: Oman is a sultanate on the south-eastern coast of the Arabian Peninsula, in the Middle East.

clue.text: Element in enthusiastic type that's upset doddery gents

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so the word is read backwards in this down clue

parts.note: a nut is an enthusiast, as in a fitness nut

indicators.note: doddery means shaky, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A keen fellow who is disturbed by unsteady old men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's upset' turns NUT into TUN; 'doddery' rearranges GENTS to GSTEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Tungsten is a chemical element, a hard metal used in lamp filaments.

clue.text: Husband is given trouble in wintry weather

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband in genealogies
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A husband is bothered by the cold winter conditions.
explanation.definitionFit: Hail is pellets of ice falling from the sky, a typical cold-season precipitation.

clue.text: Traveller in China in a good year has to make grovelling statement?

indicators.note: in places one piece within the others

parts.note: Marco Polo travelled to China in the thirteenth century

explanation.surface: A traveller in China in a fortunate year must issue a humble statement.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'in' puts POLO inside A + G + Y.
explanation.definitionFit: An apology is an expression of regret, which may be humble and abject.

clue.text: Poignant article probing countryside pursuit

indicators.note: probing means poking into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: hunting is a traditional rural pastime
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A moving newspaper piece investigating rural blood sports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'probing' puts A inside HUNTING.
explanation.definitionFit: A haunting melody or image lingers in the mind and stirs emotion, which is what poignant describes.

clue.text: US actor flips in charge of a wandering lot?

indicators.note: flips means turns over, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Matt Damon is an American actor

explanation.surface: An American film star turns upside down while leading a roving band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flips' turns DAMON into NOMAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomadic describes peoples who roam from place to place with no fixed home.

clue.text: Soprano in Paris before knowledgeable figure

parts.note: avant is French for before

explanation.surface: A singer in Paris preceding an expert.
explanation.definitionFit: A savant is a learned person, a scholar of great erudition.

clue.text: Catch normal basis for employment?

definitions.meaning: to ... an illness is to catch it
a ... of employment is the agreement on which a job usually rests

explanation.surface: Seizing on the usual grounds for hiring someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Contract means both to catch a disease and a binding agreement, such as the one governing a job.

clue.text: Dark place to go in dilapidated gym

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
dilapidated means falling apart, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the loo is the toilet, where one 'goes'

explanation.surface: A grim toilet in a run-down gymnasium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dilapidated' scrambles the gym and 'in' puts the British slang for toilet inside it; a 'place to go' is a lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloomy describes a place with little light, so it can stand for dark.

clue.text: Source notes criminal describing where shooting takes place?

indicators.note: criminal means bent or crooked, so the letters are twisted round

explanation.surface: An informant's notes are illegal, relating to a shooting.
explanation.walkthrough: The tail is a second, cryptic hint: ON SET is where a film shoot happens.
explanation.definitionFit: The onset of something is its start, its point of origin.

clue.text: Eastern Europeans given a role to be very different

parts.note: Poles are people from Poland
a part is a role in a play

explanation.surface: Polish actors cast in a part prove to be quite unlike each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Poles apart is an idiom for being completely opposed, as far from each other as the North and South Poles.

clue.text: Set of players expressed dejection, we're told

indicators.note: what we are told we hear, so this is a sound-alike

parts.note: to sigh is to breathe out audibly in sadness

explanation.surface: The team let out a sigh, so the report goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we're told' signals a homophone: SIGHED sounds like SIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A side is a team, the players fielded together in a match.

clue.text: Growth clearly suspect at the margins

indicators.note: the margins are the edges, so the first and last letters of each word

explanation.surface: A lump is plainly suspicious around its edges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the margins' takes C and Y from CLEARLY and S and T from SUSPECT.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyst is a sac-like swelling in the body, a kind of abnormal growth.

clue.text: Observe one with a ticket in a mess

indicators.note: a mess is disorder, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone notices their parking ticket lying among the clutter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a mess' is the anagram signal on ONE and A TICKET.
explanation.definitionFit: To take notice is to pay heed to, to observe something.
